whatChanged.headline: Salesforce's $5.66 Billion Bet on Marketing That Reacts to You
whatChanged.headlineZh: Salesforce 拟以 56.6 亿美元收购 Braze，让营销消息跟着你的行为走
intro: You look at a pair of shoes in an app. A little later, a message arrives with just the right offer. That timing is the kind of technology Salesforce is paying billions to get.
introZh: 你在 App 里看了一双鞋，过了一会儿，优惠消息就来了。Salesforce 正准备花几十亿美元，买下让这种消息在恰当时刻出现的技术。

sections.heading: What happened?
paragraphs: On October 20, Salesforce announced an agreement to acquire Braze, a customer-engagement software company, for about $5.66 billion in enterprise value. The proposed deal would pay Braze Class A shareholders $47.50 a share in cash. Braze says it serves around 2,770 customers, including Canva, Instacart and Venmo.
paragraphsZh: 10 月 20 日，Salesforce 宣布与客户互动软件公司 Braze 达成收购协议，按企业价值计算，交易金额约 56.6 亿美元。按协议，Braze 的 A 类普通股股东每股可获得 47.50 美元现金。Braze 称自己有约 2,770 家客户，包括 Canva、Instacart 和 Venmo。

sections.heading: What exactly is Salesforce buying?
paragraphs: According to Salesforce and Braze, Braze helps brands respond to what customers do in real time: browsing a website, using an app or making a purchase. The companies say its software coordinates messages across email, apps, websites and services such as WhatsApp. They also say BrazeAI adds tools to help choose the message, offer, channel and timing. Salesforce wants to combine that with its customer data and AI-agent products, but the integration has not happened yet.
paragraphsZh: 据 Salesforce 和 Braze 两家公司介绍，Braze 的软件能根据用户的实时行为调整沟通方式，比如浏览网站、使用 App 或完成购买。两家公司表示，这套软件可以协调邮件、App、网站和 WhatsApp 等渠道上的消息。据两家公司介绍，BrazeAI 进一步帮助企业选择内容、优惠、发送渠道和时机。Salesforce 希望把这些能力与自己的客户数据及 AI Agent 产品结合，但目前还没有完成整合。

sections.heading: Why is this an AI story?
sections.headingZh: 这为什么是一条 AI 新闻？
paragraphs: Generating a marketing message is becoming easier. The harder commercial question is what to say, to whom, and when. Salesforce is betting that software able to act on live customer signals will become more valuable as businesses adopt AI.
paragraphsZh: 用 AI 写一条营销消息越来越容易，真正难的是决定发给谁、说什么、什么时候发。Salesforce 赌的是：能根据用户实时行为采取行动的软件，会越来越值钱。

sections.heading: What happens next?
paragraphs: This is an agreement, not a completed takeover. Salesforce expects the transaction to close in its fiscal year 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. For consumers, the result could be more useful reminders—or messages that feel a little too well timed.
paragraphsZh: 这只是已签署的收购协议，交易尚未完成。Salesforce 预计在其 2028 财年完成交易，仍需获得股东及监管批准。对普通人来说，未来可能收到更有用的提醒，也可能觉得广告来得有点过于及时。

whatChanged.ending: When marketing gets better at reading the moment, will it feel more helpful—or harder to ignore?
whatChanged.endingZh: 当营销越来越会挑时机，我们会觉得它更贴心，还是更难躲开？

stayCurious.categoryZh: 新加坡 / 城市生活 / 公共住房
stayCurious.headline: Why Do So Many Singapore HDB Blocks Leave the Ground Floor Open?
stayCurious.headlineZh: 为什么新加坡很多组屋的一楼都是空的？
intro: Land in Singapore is precious. So why do so many HDB blocks stand on pillars, with no apartments on the ground floor? That open space has a name: the void deck.
introZh: 新加坡土地这么贵，为什么很多组屋的一楼却没有住宅，只留下一排柱子和空地？这种空间有个名字：void deck，组屋底层的公共空间。

sections.heading: Was it designed for the weather?
sections.headingZh: 是为了适应热带天气吗？
paragraphs: That's part of the story. Open ground floors allow air to move through buildings, offer shelter from sun and rain, and can help with flood prevention. In 1967, planner Alan Choe described an open transition level in a mixed-use HDB complex in Chinatown as a buffer to improve cross-ventilation and make the building look less bulky. He separately proposed using the space for play and recreation. The idea later spread through public housing.
paragraphsZh: 这是原因之一。开放式底层有利于空气流通，能遮阳挡雨，也有助于防洪。1967 年，规划师 Alan Choe 曾介绍牛车水一个组屋商住综合项目中的开放式过渡楼层：它能促进空气流通，也让建筑看起来不那么厚重。他还另外建议将这片空间用于儿童玩耍和休闲活动。后来，这种设计逐渐在公共住房中普及。

sections.heading: What about the children?
paragraphs: In 1973, then National Development Minister E. W. Barker decided to keep the ground floors of public housing blocks open, especially for children, because recreational space was scarce. Over time, void decks became places for neighbours to meet, and for events such as Malay weddings and Chinese funeral wakes.
paragraphsZh: 1973 年，时任国家发展部长 E. W. Barker 决定将公共住房的底层保留为开放空间，尤其供孩子们使用，因为当时缺少游乐空间。之后，void deck 逐渐成为邻居碰面、举办马来婚礼或华人丧礼的场所。

sections.heading: But doesn't leaving a floor empty cost money?
sections.headingZh: 可是一楼不卖房，不就少赚钱吗？
paragraphs: Potentially, yes. Singapore's Urban Redevelopment Authority counts void decks as gross floor area. Where a development has a fixed floor-area limit, open communal space can compete with space for apartments or shops. But that doesn't mean every block could simply add another full floor of homes; the trade-off depends on its design and planning limits.
paragraphsZh: 可能确实有机会成本。新加坡市区重建局（URA）规定，void deck 也计入建筑总楼面面积。如果一个项目的总楼面面积有上限，留给公共空间的面积就可能与住宅或商铺竞争。但这不代表每栋楼都能直接多盖一整层住宅，具体还取决于建筑设计和规划限制。

sections.heading: So what does the space give back?
sections.headingZh: 那这些空间换来了什么？
paragraphs: One covered area can serve many households in different ways, on different days. It isn't empty in the way an unused apartment is empty.
paragraphsZh: 同一片有遮蔽的空间，可以在不同日子服务很多家庭。它看起来空着，却不是没有用途。

stayCurious.ending: In a city where space is expensive, the ground floor may be worth more to residents when nobody owns a flat on it.
stayCurious.endingZh: 在寸土寸金的城市里，一楼没有住户，反而可能让更多住户用得上它。
